Transport is the --transport flag (stdio|http|https|proxy), default proxy since ADR-0020. MCP_TRANSPORT and AIRACCOON_DATA_ROOT do NOT exist - ServerConfig records that the env layer was removed by the single-channel ruling, and McpServerFactory injects the data root via WebApplicationFactory.UseSetting, not the environment
sqlite-memory's content-hash dedup is global — cross-context duplicates need preserve_duplicate_paths=1 + distinct logical paths
Dapper 2.1.79 parameter binding is case-sensitive against SQL param names and its record ctor matching chokes on nullable params — alias columns and use a settable DTO
sqlite-memory/vector/sync are native SQLite extensions loaded via Microsoft.Data.Sqlite LoadExtension; deferred embeddings (defer_embeddings=1) let writes work before any model is configured
MCP protocol CallToolResult.IsError is null on success (absent), true only on failure — assert ShouldNotBe(true), not ShouldBe(false)
Bare `ai-raccoon` is a proxy: it opens no bank, resolves no key and loads no ONNX model. `--transport stdio` is the in-process server and the escape hatch when a backend cannot start

`serve` mints <data-root>/mcp-token (0600) BEFORE it binds, so a port that answers guarantees the file exists; the probe accepts 401 as proof of a live server so it still recognises one across data roots

/mcp and /shutdown accept the loopback token in either envelope: X-AiRaccoon-Token or Authorization: Bearer *** one credential compared with FixedTimeEquals on both paths and neither shadowing the other. /mcp alone renders a second 401 body for a credential that was presented but did not match; /shutdown keeps one body for every failure because ADR-0022 pins the refusal not to reveal whether a token exists. `serve --mcp-entry` prints a headers map carrying ${AIRACCOON_MCP_TOKEN}, never a live token - Hermes resolves it from ~/.hermes/.env, Claude Code from the environment, and an unset variable in Claude Code warns in `claude mcp list` but still sends the literal placeholder.
